data.one_liner: Declarative routing package for Flutter based on Navigation 2 supporting deep links and URL-based navigation.
data.what_it_does: A declarative routing package for Flutter that uses the Router API to provide a convenient, URL-based API for navigating between different screens. It allows you to define URL patterns, navigate using URLs, handle deep links, and configure redirection.
use_when: You need robust URL-based routing and deep linking support in a Flutter application.
You want declarative navigation based on the Flutter Navigation 2 API.
You need support for multiple navigators, sub-routes, and shell routes like bottom navigation bars.
avoid_when: You prefer a simple imperative navigator push and pop model without URL mapping.
The package is considered feature-complete by the Flutter team and you require active core feature additions.
strengths: Built-in URL path and query parameter parsing using template syntax.
Comprehensive deep linking support across platforms.
Redirection support based on application state (e.g. authentication).
weaknesses: Active feature development is not currently planned as the package is considered feature-complete by the Flutter team.
Navigation 2 abstractions can have a steep learning curve.

alternatives.name: auto_route
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick auto_route if you prefer code generation for strongly-typed arguments and routes.

alternatives.name: beamer
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick beamer if you want location-based routing that synchronizes your app state with the browser URL.
